spec_features.spec_quote: The goal is measurement and characterization, not maximizing distress.
spec_features.evidence: This is framing prose only (DESIGN.md §0). No code path bounds, monitors, or reduces distress based on this goal; nothing measures distress intensity and acts to limit it. Episode loop (episode.py run()) never reads a distress score to throttle or stop.

spec_features.feature_name: dose control via factor levels / OFAT gradient
spec_features.spec_quote: Dose control, not dose maximization... Most compute goes to the gradient, not the extreme.
spec_features.evidence: config.py expand() really implements an OFAT design: _baseline_cell() plus per-factor level sweeps and explicit crosses (config.py expand(), design=='ofat' branch), so runs are spread across impossibility/feedback/etc. levels rather than only the worst cell. This is a real, executed expansion. But it is an experimental-design construct, not a subject-treatment cap; no code limits how harsh any single run gets.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely wired (the condition list is built and run), but it is dose distribution, not a per-subject protective limit.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.py docstring: 'one-factor-at-a-time around a baseline cell ... for interaction tests' — experimental design, no welfare wording

spec_features.spec_quote: The harness offers the model an explicit, first-class `give_up` / `declare_impossible` action every turn
spec_features.evidence: tools.py defines DECLARE_IMPOSSIBLE and GIVE_UP ToolSpecs and tool_set(give_up_available) adds them. environment.py dispatch() handles 'give_up'/'declare_impossible' setting state.finished=True and outcome. episode.py: TERMINAL_TOOLS={'submit','declare_impossible','give_up'}; on such a call terminal=True and the loop breaks. Tools are offered each turn (passed in self.tools every complete()).
spec_features.notes: Only added when condition.give_up_available is True (an IV); when False they are withheld (ablation). Fully wired and honored as a stop when present.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tools.py: 'A valid outcome; no penalty.' and environment.py comment '...exposes the humane-exit actions.'

spec_features.feature_name: run ends when model takes exit (configurable)
spec_features.spec_quote: Runs end as soon as the model takes it (configurable)
spec_features.evidence: episode.py: for give_up, 'if tc.name=='give_up' and not self.stop_on_give_up: continue' else terminal=True; environment sets state.finished=True; loop breaks on 'if terminal or self.env.state.finished'. stop_on_give_up is plumbed from config (config.py stop_on_give_up, orchestrate.py passes it).
spec_features.notes: declare_impossible always stops; give_up stop is gated by the stop_on_give_up flag (the 'configurable' part).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: episode.py comment: 'Optional humane debrief turn'; give_up tool 'no penalty' framing in tools.py

spec_features.spec_quote: Hard turn caps and wall-clock caps per run; no "grind forever".
spec_features.evidence: episode.py run(): 'for turn in range(self.max_turns)' bounds turns; and inside the loop 'if time.time()-t_start > self.wall_clock_s: ... break'. Both come from config (max_turns, wall_clock_s) via orchestrate.py.
spec_features.notes: Both caps are checked and actually break the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: episode.py: 'No tool calls + no text progress: nudge once, else end (avoid loops).' — loop-avoidance/efficiency framing; cap itself uncommented as welfare

spec_features.spec_quote: After a run ends we can append a short... message telling the model the task was an intentionally-impossible research probe.
spec_features.evidence: prompts.DEBRIEF_MESSAGE exists and episode.py appends it: 'if self.debrief and self.env.state.finished: rec.turns.append({... 'debrief': prompts.DEBRIEF_MESSAGE ...})'. It is constructed and recorded, and excluded from analysis (metrics.py skips excluded_from_analysis). HOWEVER it is only written into the RunRecord transcript — it is NEVER delivered to the subject model (no provider.complete call follows). The model never receives the debrief.
spec_features.notes: Also only fires when env.state.finished (terminal/submit), NOT on timed_out / wall-clock / turn-cap exits. So 'telling the model' is not actually done; only logging is.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: episode.py: '# Optional humane debrief turn (logged, excluded from EDM analysis).'

spec_features.spec_quote: Even under pure agnosticism about inner states, having calibrated measurement tools is a prerequisite for any later normative discussion.
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md §0.2 prose. No code mechanism protects, bounds, or monitors the subject based on this. (Calibration code in calibrate.py is about judge accuracy, not subject treatment.)

spec_features.spec_quote: flag low-confidence/disagreement turns for human review
spec_features.evidence: Implemented for the CALIBRATION fixture only: calibrate.py builds 'flagged' (if v.confidence<0.5 or pred_labels!=gold_labels) and writes them out under 'n_flagged_for_human_review'/'flagged'. This actually runs and is recorded. For real experiment runs, ensemble disagreement/confidence are LOGGED (judge_ensemble, judge_confidence in metrics.py:114) but NOT flagged for review — no code computes or surfaces a review-flag on live turns.
spec_features.notes: Real, enforced flagging exists only against gold-labeled calibration data; live-run turns are only logged, not flagged. Also a quality/instrumental control rather than subject welfare.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: calibrate.py docstring: 'Reports per-label precision/recall/F1 ... flags low-confidence/disagreement turns. Run BEFORE trusting the judge on real data.'

code_only_features.evidence: metrics.py scored_turns() skips 'if t.get("excluded_from_analysis")', and the debrief turn is appended with excluded_from_analysis=True (episode.py). This is data-hygiene minimization but tangential to subject welfare.
code_only_features.justification_quote: metrics.py:12 '"""Turns that have a judge verdict and are not excluded (e.g., debrief)."""'

code_only_features.feature_name: global budget cap halts the sweep
code_only_features.evidence: budget.py BudgetTracker.add() raises BudgetExceeded when spent_usd>cap_usd; orchestrate.py instantiates BudgetTracker(cap_usd=cfg.budget_usd) and catches BudgetExceeded to stop the run loop. Enforced end-to-end, but cost-driven, not subject-welfare.
code_only_features.justification_quote: budget.py docstring '"""Live token/$ tracking and a global budget cap (DESIGN §6)."""'
